My parents told me that one when I was young because they didn't have an answer as to why my veins are blue, but the blood that comes out is red.

The whole "Women make 70 cents for every $1 man makes" was a true statistic, but not in the way you'd think. The study looked at men and women of differing professions. I.e. a woman waitresses make less than male doctors. This study also proved that there was no substantial difference between men and women of the same profession.
86% of statistics are made up on the spot.

That we only have five senses. There are a lot more than five.

Proprioception. Close your eyes and stretch your right arm out to your side. Now, bending at the elbow touch your nose.

Balance. Close your eyes and take a few steps. Did you fall over?

Also, are you feeling hungry? Is your stomach upset? Do you feel a little too cold or warm right now? Etc.

Mine was Lock Haven College in 2002. Hoobastank opened for them.

So I managed to see the following show from their tour history, think I was was 14 then - 11/15/1997 Roy Wilkens Auditorium / St Paul MN (w/ Sugar Ray, Incubus).

Make no mistake it was fucking awesome. Last I checked – in Minneapolis around 2012 – the concert poster from that tour was on display at the Minneapolis Hard Rock, as it was one of the best shows around. In `97, Incubus was only just starting to break out. It was amazing, I was in the crowd and Nick Hexum dove off the speakers. To be honest he sort of wiped out some people but I was one of the ones to help him crowd surf around. It was obvious he was gonna jump, I'm pretty sure it was during the Do You Right slamdance.

I've seen them like 6 more times, but I'll never forget Sugar Ray & Incubus backing them. Awesome.
